characteristics.roast: Rice is roasted; tea leaves remain unroasted
characteristics.harvestSeason: Based on regular season harvests (second/third flush, bancha)

description.short: Green tea blended with roasted brown rice — comforting, nutty, and savory everyday beverage
description.overview: A blend of steamed green tea leaves with toasted puffed brown rice, where occasional grains pop open like miniature popcorn — hence its playful Western nickname.
description.leaf: Combination of dark green tea leaves with golden-brown toasted rice and white popped kernels
description.aroma: Toasted grain, nutty, warm basmati aroma
description.taste: Mellow, nutty, savory sweetness from rice carbohydrates softening the brisk green tea astringency
description.processing: Production of base green tea (sencha or bancha) → separate high-temperature roasting of brown rice until puffed → careful proportioned blending

history.origin: Originally invented by budget-conscious tea drinkers as a clever way to extend expensive tea leaves with affordable roasted rice during lean economic times.
history.development: Over time, the blend moved from economic necessity to a beloved comfort tea celebrated for its warming, savory profile.
history.modern: Today genmaicha is one of Japan's most popular daily staples and a globally recognized comfort tea, widely enjoyed alongside meals.
interestingFacts: Nicknamed 'popcorn tea' because grains of rice pop open during roasting, creating white puffed blossoms scattered through the blend.
A popular luxury variation called 'Matcha-iri Genmaicha' coats the leaves and rice in vivid green matcha powder, giving an emerald liquor and rich umami kick.
